newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China, Britain agree on HK Exchange Fund transfer.
newsitem.headline: China, Britain agree on HK Exchange Fund transfer.

text.p: China and Britain have signed a pact to transfer Hong Kong's Exchange Fund to the new local administration after the colony reverts to Beijing's rule next year, the Hong Kong government said on Wednesday.
Hong Kong will be handed back at midnight on June 30, 1997, and will become a Special Administrative Region (SAR) of China.

The "agreed minute" on the Exchange Fund, which is used to underpin the Hong Kong dollar, was signed in Hong Kong by diplomatic negotiators in the Sino-British Joint Liaison Group, which is charged with hammering out the transition arrangements.
The minute says the entire Exchange Fund will be transferred to the SAR government and will be managed in accordance with the relevant SAR laws, a government statement said.

The minute also says all documents, contracts and agreements signed by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, the territory's de facto central bank, up to June 30 next year shall continue to be valid after that date and will be protected by SAR laws.
The government said the arrangements would ensure continuity in the management of the Exchange Fund, leaving no gap in the transfer process or doubts over the Fund's ownership.
China and Britain "have agreed to appoint a reputable international audit firm in Hong Kong to audit the accounts of the Exchange Fund", it added.
They have also agreed to continue to strengthen consultation and cooperation on matters related to the Fund's transfer, the government said.
The Exchange Fund stood at HK$485 billion at the end of June. The Hong Kong dollar is pegged at HK$7.8 to the dollar.
